hook.line: Late at night, Don Hernando asks Tomás what he would do with a second chance. The answer starts with a Spanish that is not about today.
hook.es: Si volviera a nacer, estudiaría otra cosa.
hook.en: If I had my life over again, I'd study something else.

rule:
To imagine a different life or a second chance, start with *si* + the imperfect subjunctive, then use the conditional.

*Si volviera a nacer, estudiaría otra cosa.*

The three openers differ only in scope:
*Si volviera a nacer…* (your whole life)
*Si pudiera devolver el tiempo…* (one moment)
*Si tuviera otra oportunidad…* (one more try)

The *si* part never takes the conditional: not *si volvería*. The other part never takes the present: not *estudio*.

English is the same, "if I had… I would". Spanish just makes the first verb special: *volviera*, *pudiera*, *tuviera*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a second-conditional (unreal) sentence: *si* + imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional.

yourTurn.why: After *si*, imagining, use the imperfect subjunctive: *volviera*.

pitfalls.wrong: Si volvería a nacer, estudiaría otra cosa.
pitfalls.right: Si volviera a nacer, estudiaría otra cosa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The *si* part takes the subjunctive, never the conditional.

pitfalls.wrong: Si volviera a nacer, estudio otra cosa.
pitfalls.right: Si volviera a nacer, estudiaría otra cosa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The result needs the conditional, because it is imagined.

pitfalls.wrong: Si podía devolver el tiempo, le diría que la quiero.
pitfalls.right: Si pudiera devolver el tiempo, le diría que la quiero.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For something unreal, use *pudiera*, not *podía*.

personal: Finish the idea about your own life: *Si pudiera devolver el tiempo…* or *Si volviera a nacer…*.
